# Zig Guide Live

> A Zig tutorial and cookbook. Each build compiles and runs every snippet against current Zig master, and the snippets run in your browser as WebAssembly.

Every snippet on this site is compiled and executed by CI against current
Zig master on every build, including a nightly run against that day's
compiler. Code here that no longer compiles fails the build and is fixed,
so it does not go stale the way a tutorial pinned to an old release does.
This tracks Zig master, not a tagged release, and it is an unofficial
community guide with no affiliation to the Zig Software Foundation.

Each chapter link below is the Markdown source. Replace `.md` with a
trailing slash for the HTML page, which additionally runs the snippets in
the browser as WebAssembly.

- [Full guide as one file](https://www.ziglang.in/llms-full.txt): every chapter concatenated, code included.
- [Chapter index](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/): the same list as HTML.

## Foundations

The language and its standard library. Start here.

### Getting Started

Install a Zig master build, compile and run your first program, run tests, and learn what changed since the last tagged release.

- [Installation](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/getting-started/installation.md): How to get a Zig master build, and why this guide needs one.
- [Hello World](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/getting-started/hello-world.md): Your first Zig program, and the reason that main now takes an argument.
- [Run Tests](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/getting-started/running-tests.md): Tests are part of the language.
- [Migrate from an Older Zig](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/getting-started/coming-from-older-zig.md): The changes between the last stable releases and the master that this guide uses.
- [What Changed in Zig 0.17](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/getting-started/zig-0-17.md): The changes between 0.16.0 and 0.17.0, checked on the two compilers.

### Language

Runnable Zig language chapters: integers, floats, pointers, slices, optionals, error unions, structs, unions, enums, switch, loops, comptime and vectors.

- [Assignment](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/assignment.md): const by default, and var only when you must change the value.
- [Arrays](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/arrays.md): Fixed-length sequences whose length is part of the type.
- [If Expressions](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/if-expressions.md): No truthiness: if takes a bool.
- [While Loops](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/while-loops.md): Conditions, continue expressions, and loops that produce values.
- [For Loops](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/for-loops.md): Iterate over sequences and ranges, never over a bare counter.
- [Functions](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/functions.md): Immutable parameters and explicit discards.
- [Defer](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/defer.md): Cleanup code that runs on each path out of a scope.
- [Errors](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/errors.md): Errors are values in a union, not exceptions.
- [Switch](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/switch.md): Exhaustive by construction.
- [Runtime Safety](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/runtime-safety.md): Checked illegal behaviour, and where the checks go.
- [Pointers](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/pointers.md): Single-item pointers that are never null.
- [Pointer Sized Integers](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/pointer-sized-integers.md): usize, isize, and why they are not the same as u64.
- [Many-item Pointers](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/many-item-pointers.md): [*]T: a pointer to an unknown number of items.
- [Slices](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/slices.md): A pointer and a length, together.
- [Enums](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/enums.md): Named values, fixed tags, and methods.
- [Structs](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/structs.md): Layout, defaults, and methods.
- [Unions](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/unions.md): One of several types, in one allocation.
- [Integer Rules](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/integer-rules.md): Arbitrary widths, explicit narrowing, chosen overflow behaviour.
- [Floats](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/floats.md): IEEE-754 types and explicit conversions.
- [Labelled Blocks](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/labelled-blocks.md): Blocks that produce a value.
- [Labelled Loops](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/labelled-loops.md): Break or continue an outer loop by name.
- [Labelled Switch](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/labelled-switch.md): A switch that you can jump back into with a new value.
- [Loops as Expressions](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/loops-as-expressions.md): The else branch gives the value when no break runs.
- [Payload Captures](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/payload-captures.md): The |value| syntax that unwraps all wrapper types.
- [Optionals](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/optionals.md): The Zig answer to null, checked by the compiler.
- [Comptime](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/comptime.md): Usual Zig code that the compiler runs.
- [Interfaces](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/interfaces.md): No interface keyword. Four shapes instead, and what each shape costs.
- [Inline Loops](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/inline-loops.md): Unrolled loops where each iteration can have a different type.
- [Opaque](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/opaque.md): Types with unknown size, used through pointers only.
- [Anonymous Structs](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/anonymous-structs.md): Struct literals with an inferred type, and tuples.
- [Sentinel Termination](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/sentinel-termination.md): Sequences that end in a known marker.
- [Vectors](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/vectors.md): SIMD with ordinary operators.
- [Imports](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/imports.md): Files are structs, and pub controls the boundary.
- [Array Recipes](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/array-recipes.md): Grids, lookup tables made at compile time, and how to get an array from a slice.
- [Slice Recipes](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/language-basics/slice-recipes.md): Reverse, rotate, shift and search a slice, in place and without an allocator.

### Comptime

Zig comptime by example: lookup tables that the compiler builds, @typeInfo reflection, @Struct and @Enum, dispatch, @compileError, and three projects: units of measure, an argument parser and an event bus.

- [Know What the Compiler Knows](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/metaprogramming/compiler-knows.md): The rule that decides which values the compiler can use, and four ways to use them.
- [Build Lookup Tables](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/metaprogramming/lookup-tables.md): The compiler calculates a CRC-32 table, and the program checks it against the standard library.
- [Read a Type](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/metaprogramming/read-a-type.md): Use @typeInfo to list the fields of a struct, an enum and a union, then write a generic diff.
- [Make a Type](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/metaprogramming/make-a-type.md): Make integer, struct, enum and tuple types from comptime values, and write a Partial(T) patch type.
- [Dispatch with Comptime](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/metaprogramming/dispatch.md): Connect each tag of an enum to its handler at compile time, with a switch or with a table.
- [Reject Bad Input with @compileError](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/metaprogramming/compile-error.md): Check the type that a generic function receives, and stop the build with a message that names the problem.
- [Parse Strings at Compile Time](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/metaprogramming/parse-strings.md): Parse a route pattern during compilation, and make a struct type for its parameters.
- [Know the Limits](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/metaprogramming/limits.md): What comptime code cannot do, what to use instead, and what comptime costs.
- [Project: Units of Measure](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/metaprogramming/units.md): A number type that carries its unit. Metres times metres is an area, and metres plus seconds does not compile.
- [Project: Parse Arguments from a Struct](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/metaprogramming/args.md): The fields of a struct are the options. The compiler makes the parser and the help text.
- [Project: A Typed Event Bus](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/metaprogramming/event-bus.md): Handlers are plain functions. The bus reads their parameter types and connects each one to its event during compilation.

### Standard Library

Zig std by example: allocators, ArrayList, hash maps, JSON, the Io interface, readers and writers, crypto, formatting and sort.

- [The Io Interface](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/io-interface.md): Each operation that can block takes an Io. The caller selects how the Io works.
- [Allocators](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/allocators.md): Explicit memory management, with the allocator given as a value.
- [ArrayList](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/arraylist.md): The array that can grow, now unmanaged.
- [Hash Maps](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/hash-maps.md): Key-value storage, and the getOrPut pattern.
- [Stacks](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/stacks.md): ArrayList from one end, or no allocator at all.
- [PriorityQueue](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/priority-queue.md): A binary heap where the comparator is part of the type.
- [MultiArrayList](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/multi-array-list.md): A struct of arrays, with a memory layout that helps the cache.
- [Bit Sets and Enum Collections](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/bit-sets.md): A set of small integers in a word, and containers with an enum as the key.
- [Strings](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/strings.md): Search, trim, split, join. All of these functions are in std.mem.
- [Unicode](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/unicode.md): A string is bytes until you select UTF-8 support.
- [Formatting](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/formatting.md): Format strings that the compiler checks.
- [Advanced Formatting](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/advanced-formatting.md): Custom format methods, and the format specifiers that changed.
- [Parsing and Encoding](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/parsing-and-encoding.md): Text to numbers, and bytes to hex or base64.
- [String Recipes](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/string-recipes.md): Padding, runtime concatenation, and the std.mem and std.ascii calls that the Strings chapter does not show.
- [Unicode Recipes](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/unicode-recipes.md): Truncate on a character boundary, decode one codepoint, and convert to UTF-16.
- [Readers and Writers](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/readers-and-writers.md): The buffered Reader and Writer interfaces introduced in Zig 0.15.
- [JSON](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/json.md): Parse JSON into real types, and write the types back as JSON.
- [Filesystem](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/filesystem.md): Each disk operation now takes an Io.
- [Command-Line Arguments](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/command-line.md): How to read argv and the environment through std.process.
- [Sorting](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/sorting.md): In-place sorts with a comparator that you supply.
- [Iterators](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/iterators.md): A convention, not an interface.
- [Random Numbers](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/random-numbers.md): Seeded generators that you give to your code as arguments.
- [Crypto](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/crypto.md): Hashes, MACs, and constant-time comparison.
- [Time](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/time.md): The clocks are behind the Io interface. The constants and calendars are in std.time.
- [Logging](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/logging.md): One log function, selected at the root and known at compile time.
- [Testing](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/standard-library/testing.md): The assertions other than expect, and the allocator that finds leaks.

### Working with Files

How to read and write files in Zig with std.Io: full files and lines, text and binary formats, seek and positional reads, CSV, directories and errors.

- [Open, Read, Close](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/files/open-read-close.md): Three ways to read a file, and what each one does when the file is larger than you expect.
- [Read Line by Line](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/files/read-lines.md): A line loop over a file, three types of line ending, a line longer than the buffer, and a large file through a small buffer.
- [Write Text Files](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/files/write-text.md): Truncate or keep, create only if new, append, the flush that the program forgot, and how to replace a file in one step.
- [Binary Files](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/files/binary-files.md): A small binary format with a header, written one field at a time, and a reader that checks each byte that it did not write.
- [Random Access](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/files/random-access.md): A file of records of fixed size. Read record N and not the records before it, change one record in place, and make the file larger and smaller.
- [Read CSV](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/files/csv-read.md): A CSV reader as a state machine with four states, a trace of each byte, the errors of a comma split, and line numbers.
- [Write CSV](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/files/csv-write.md): Quote a field only when it needs quotes, write each quote in it two times, and read the output again to prove the writer.
- [Directories](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/files/directories.md): Create a tree of directories, list one level, walk all levels, rename a directory and delete the full tree.
- [When Things Go Wrong](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/files/failures.md): What stat tells you, six file operations that fail and the error from each, messages for a person, and how to delete a half-written file.

### Data Structures

Build containers in Zig: a growable array, a linked list, generic containers, the intrusive lists in std, a binary search tree, AVL and a hash map.

- [A Growable Array](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/data-structures/growable-array.md): A length, a capacity, and one rule for what occurs when the length reaches the capacity.
- [A Linked List by Hand](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/data-structures/linked-list.md): The smallest structure that needs an allocator, an optional pointer and a deinit with the correct order.
- [Make It Generic](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/data-structures/generic-list.md): Zig has no generics syntax. A generic container is a function that takes a type and returns a type at compile time.
- [The Lists in std Are Intrusive](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/data-structures/std-lists.md): std.SinglyLinkedList is not generic and does not hold your data. Put its node in your struct and get back to the struct with @fieldParentPtr.
- [A Binary Search Tree](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/data-structures/bst.md): Two pointers instead of one give ordered iteration and O(log n) lookup, on a condition that the structure does not enforce.
- [Keep It Balanced](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/data-structures/avl.md): Store a height, check it after each insert, and repair the shape with a local rotation. Four cases, and each case has five lines or fewer.
- [A Hash Map from Scratch](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/data-structures/hash-map.md): Open addressing with linear probing, growth at 75%, and the tombstone. The tombstone looks like a hack, but it makes delete work.

### Concurrency

Concurrency in Zig with std.Io: async, Future, Group, cancellation, Select, queues, locks, atomics, OS threads, std.Thread today, and a batch runner.

- [Async, Future and Group](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/concurrency/async-future-group.md): async, Future, and Group, all through the Io interface.
- [Cancellation](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/concurrency/cancellation.md): How to stop a task that runs, and the cancellation points that make it possible.
- [Select](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/concurrency/select.md): Wait for the task that completes first, and cancel the other tasks.
- [Queues](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/concurrency/queues.md): Io.Queue as a bounded channel between tasks, with close and back pressure.
- [Locks and Semaphores](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/concurrency/locks.md): RwLock, Semaphore and Condition, for the cases where a Mutex is not sufficient.
- [Atomics](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/concurrency/atomics.md): One counter, all the ways to add one to it, and the purpose of the ordering argument.
- [Threads](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/concurrency/threads.md): Real OS threads, and why this page cannot run in your browser.
- [Migrate from `std.Thread`](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/concurrency/coming-from-std-thread.md): Seven names that Zig removed, where each one went, and why lock can now fail.
- [Choose an Io](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/concurrency/choosing-an-io.md): Threaded, the evented implementations, and how to build an Io yourself.
- [A Batch Job Runner](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/concurrency/batch-runner.md): Four workers, one batch, three kinds of shared state, and a measurement that says one thread did all of the work.

## Groundwork

What the machine does, from zero. The track assumes no C and no earlier systems work.

### Systems from Scratch

Systems programming from zero: bytes and types, overflow, addresses, the stack, memory ownership, struct layout, errors and system calls.

- [Everything Is Bytes](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/systems-from-scratch/everything-is-bytes.md): A type is not a property of the bytes. A type is an agreement about how to read the bytes.
- [Numbers Have a Size](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/systems-from-scratch/numbers-have-a-size.md): A u8 counts to 255 and stops. You decide what happens next.
- [Memory Is Numbered](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/systems-from-scratch/memory-is-numbered.md): An address is an ordinary number, and a pointer is a variable that holds an address.
- [The Stack](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/systems-from-scratch/the-stack.md): Where local variables live, and why a pointer to a local is not safe after the call returns.
- [Who Owns This Memory](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/systems-from-scratch/who-owns-this-memory.md): Memory that must stay valid after a call returns needs a request, and a person or a function must give it back.
- [Off the End](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/systems-from-scratch/off-the-end.md): A length is a value. Languages are different in who must check the length.
- [When the Checks Are Off](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/systems-from-scratch/when-checks-are-off.md): What undefined behaviour is, and what each build mode promises.
- [Strings Are Bytes](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/systems-from-scratch/strings-are-bytes.md): Zig has no string type. A literal is bytes, with a zero at the end.
- [Structs Are Layout](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/systems-from-scratch/structs-are-layout.md): Fields are next to each other in memory, and the size is not the sum of the parts.
- [Errors Are Values](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/systems-from-scratch/errors-are-values.md): Zig has no exception mechanism below your program. Thus a failure must be part of the value that a function returns.
- [Talk to the Operating System](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/systems-from-scratch/talking-to-the-os.md): Your program gets streams that it did not open, and it must return a status.

## Systems

Zig and the world outside the process: networks, builds, C, wasm and pixels.

### Operating System

How Zig uses the operating system: file descriptors, the standard streams, the environment, child processes, pipes, signals, and exit and defer.

- [A File Descriptor Is a Number](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/os/file-descriptors.md): Each thing that the operating system gives you to read or write is an integer.
- [The Three Standard Streams](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/os/standard-streams.md): The buffer belongs to your writer, not to the descriptor under the writer.
- [The Environment](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/os/environment.md): A map from string to string. The parent process selects the map, and your process gets the map at startup.
- [Spawn a Process](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/os/spawning.md): A child is a program, an argument list, and a status code that the parent receives.
- [Pipes Are the Child's Streams](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/os/pipes.md): A pipe is a descriptor at each end and an end-of-file in the middle.
- [Signals](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/os/signals.md): A handler interrupts you between two instructions. Set a flag and return.
- [Exit the Process](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/os/exiting.md): exit stops the process. It does not return from your program.

### Networking

Network programming in Zig, from sockets to protocols: framing, short reads, text and binary protocols, byte order, many clients, TCP, UDP, HTTP and WebSockets.

- [What a Socket Is](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/networking/what-is-a-socket.md): An address, a mode, and a handle that you read and write like a file.
- [A TCP Round Trip](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/networking/tcp-echo.md): Listen, connect, and echo through std.Io.net, all in one process.
- [Bytes Have No Edges](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/networking/short-reads.md): A read that returns 7 bytes does not tell you where a message ends.
- [Three Ways to Frame](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/networking/framing.md): Length prefix, delimiter, self-describing, and the cost of each one.
- [A Text Protocol, Both Directions](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/networking/text-protocols.md): Parse a command from bytes, and write a reply back into bytes.
- [Binary Protocols and Byte Order](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/networking/binary-protocols.md): A struct is not a wire format. Write the fields, and state which end is first.
- [Serve Many Clients](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/networking/many-clients.md): One handler for each connection through Io, thus the same source runs with threads and without threads.
- [Failure Is Ordinary](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/networking/network-errors.md): The end of a stream is not an error, and a truncated message can look like a good message.
- [UDP Datagrams](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/networking/udp-message.md): Bound sockets and discrete messages, without a connection.
- [Lost Datagrams](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/networking/packet-loss.md): Loss, duplication and reordering, made on demand so that you can see them.
- [Sequence Numbers and Acks](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/networking/sequence-numbers.md): One counter makes an invisible loss into a detected gap, and one reply gives the problem to the sender.
- [Retransmission and the Window](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/networking/retransmission.md): A timeout recovers the messages that the network lost, and a window keeps traffic in motion during the recovery.
- [An HTTP Round Trip](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/networking/http-roundtrip.md): A std.http.Server on a thread, and a std.http.Client that fetches from it, with no dependencies.
- [The WebSocket Handshake](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/networking/websocket-handshake.md): An HTTP request asks to upgrade, std.http.Server answers 101, and the checks that std leaves to your code.
- [WebSocket Frames](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/networking/websocket-frames.md): The two header bytes as packed structs, the three length forms, the client mask, and the frames that std.http.Server refuses.
- [A WebSocket Client](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/networking/websocket-client.md): A client that std does not have. It checks the handshake, masks each frame, puts fragments together, answers a ping, and closes correctly.
- [A WebSocket Server on a Socket](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/networking/websocket-server.md): std.http.Server upgrades a real TCP connection and echoes messages. The server answers pings, closes correctly, and refuses a message that is too big.

### Build System

build.zig by example: build modes, cross-compilation, dependencies in build.zig.zon, and documentation from doc comments.

- [Build Modes](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/build-system/build-modes.md): Four modes, and the cost and the benefit of each one.
- [Emit an Executable](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/build-system/emitting-an-executable.md): How to build without a build.zig.
- [Cross-compilation](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/build-system/cross-compilation.md): All targets are available when you install Zig.
- [Zig Build](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/build-system/zig-build.md): The build system is a Zig program.
- [Dependencies](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/build-system/dependencies.md): How to declare, fetch and connect a package with build.zig.zon.
- [Generate Documentation](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/build-system/generating-documentation.md): Doc comments, and the site that Zig makes from them.

### Working with C

How to call C from Zig and expose Zig to C: translate-c, C pointer types, C primitive types, and the C ABI.

- [ABI](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/working-with-c/abi.md): extern and packed, for layouts with a guarantee.
- [C Primitive Types](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/working-with-c/c-primitive-types.md): Types whose width follows the target's C ABI.
- [C Pointers](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/working-with-c/c-pointers.md): [*c]T: the pointer type translate-c emits, and why to convert it at the boundary.
- [Import C](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/working-with-c/cimport.md): translate-c, and calling C without bindings.

### WebAssembly

How to compile Zig to WebAssembly: freestanding modules, calls from JavaScript, data across the boundary, wasm in the browser, and a WASI command.

- [What WebAssembly Is](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/webassembly/what-is-wasm.md): A portable binary target for a sandboxed stack machine, and how Zig compiles to it.
- [Recipe: A WASI Command](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/webassembly/wasi-command.md): Compile a Zig program to wasm and run it from a shell under any WASI runtime.
- [Recipe: Call Zig from JavaScript](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/webassembly/export-to-js.md): Build a reactor module with exported functions and call them by name from a host.
- [Recipe: Pass Data Across the Boundary](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/webassembly/linear-memory.md): Move strings and buffers between JavaScript and wasm through shared linear memory.
- [Recipe: A Freestanding Module](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/webassembly/freestanding.md): The smallest wasm target, with no WASI and no libc, and the memory builtins that replace them.
- [Recipe: Load wasm in the Browser](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/webassembly/browser-instantiate.md): Fetch, instantiate, connect the imports and exports, and let a module call back into JavaScript.

### Graphics

Software rendering and image processing in Zig, with no graphics library: framebuffers, PNG, rasterization, blending, antialiasing, filters and scaling.

- [A Framebuffer Is an Array](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/pixel-buffers.md): Row-major layout, top-left origin, packed pixels, and a putPixel that clips.
- [Write an Image File](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/image-files.md): PPM, the image format that you can write without a library, and the one strict rule that is easy to break.
- [Write a PNG](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/png.md): A signature, three chunks and a CRC on each chunk. The writer filters the pixels, then compresses them with the zlib in the standard library.
- [Lines](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/lines.md): Bresenham's algorithm: one add and one compare per pixel, integers only.
- [Circles](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/circles.md): Compare squared distances, loop over the bounding box, and let putPixel clip.
- [Alpha Blending](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/blending.md): Source-over compositing in integers, the reason for the /255, and the reason that order is still important.
- [Linear Light](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/linear-light.md): A stored byte is not an amount of light. Decode, mix, encode, with both tables built by the compiler.
- [Rasterize Triangles](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/triangles.md): Edge functions tell inside from outside, and the same three numbers interpolate values across the face.
- [Antialiasing](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/antialiasing.md): Coverage is alpha. Do the inside test sixteen times for each pixel, and the jagged edges disappear.
- [Per-Pixel Transforms](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/per-pixel.md): Brightness, contrast, threshold and invert are all one table lookup, and brightness needs Zig's saturating add.
- [Convolution](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/convolution.md): Blur, sharpen and Sobel are one loop with different numbers in it. The two bugs are always the border and the buffer.
- [Colour Matrices](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/color-matrix.md): Grayscale, sepia and saturation are one 3x3 matrix. A chain of these matrices multiplies into one matrix before the program changes the image.
- [Histograms and Levels](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/histogram.md): Count what the image contains, and get the correction table from the counts. Auto-levels, equalization, and why to apply them to luma.
- [Median and Rank Filters](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/median.md): A convolution cannot ignore a value. Sort the neighbourhood, and one function is a denoiser, an eroder or a dilator. The index decides which.
- [Scale and Resample](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/resample.md): Nearest, bilinear and box filters, the half-pixel bug, and why a downscale without a filter makes fine detail into a solid bar.
- [Bitmap Text](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/font.md): A glyph is a small rectangle of bits. To draw text, copy those bits.
- [Sprites and Transparency](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/sprite.md): A copy of a rectangle is easy. The important feature is the decision about which pixels not to copy.
- [A Scene Graph](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/scene.md): Position each thing relative to its parent. When the parent moves, everything below the parent moves with it.
- [A Bar Chart](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/chart.md): One division changes numbers into pixels. If the division is wrong, the chart misleads the reader.
- [A Canvas Is a View](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/sub-canvas.md): Four fields, not a slice. Each routine draws inside a region, and the routine does not know that the canvas is a region.
- [Texture Mapping](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/texture.md): The triangle already interpolates. Point the triangle at a second image, and it interpolates coordinates into that image, not colours.
- [Transforms](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/transform.md): To move, turn and resize a shape is one operation. To combine them is a multiply, and you cannot select its order freely.
- [Onto the Screen](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/graphics/on-screen.md): The same buffer, given to X11 through translate-c, and what changes on Wayland.

## Cookbook

Recipes for tasks. Each recipe is a complete program that CI compiled and ran.

### How-To

A Zig cookbook of runnable recipes: JSON, SQLite, the PostgreSQL wire protocol, Redis RESP, threads and atomics, SIMD, compression and binary formats.

- [Recipe: Word Frequencies](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/word-frequency.md): Count occurrences with a hash map, then rank them with a sort.
- [Recipe: Load a JSON Config](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/json-config.md): Use defaults for absent fields, validate wrong values, and return clear errors for the other problems.
- [Recipe: A Custom JSON Serializer](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/json-custom.md): Give a struct a jsonStringify method to rename fields and add computed fields.
- [Recipe: A Binary Wire Format](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/binary-roundtrip.md): Serialize a struct to explicit bytes and back, with safe checks.
- [Recipe: JSON vs Binary, by Size](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/serialization-size.md): The same 100,000 records as JSON and as packed bytes, with exact measurements.
- [Recipe: A File-Backed To-Do Store](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/todo-store.md): Records of fixed size on disk, updated in place by id with positional reads and writes.
- [Recipe: Compress with zlib](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/zlib-compress.md): Compress and decompress in one call each through the system zlib, linked from Zig.
- [Recipe: Catch Memory Leaks](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/catching-leaks.md): Make the test suite prove that the code frees each allocation.
- [Recipe: Print Any Struct](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/struct-printer.md): Comptime reflection builds a debug printer that works for all struct types.
- [Recipe: Overflow Without Panics](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/checked-math.md): Do arithmetic on values that can be too large, without undefined behavior and without a crash.
- [Recipe: The std.math Toolbox](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/math-functions.md): Constants, trig, powers, roots, rounding, and a safe comparison of floats.
- [Recipe: A SIMD Dot Product](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/simd-sum.md): Use @Vector to process four elements in each operation, with the tail too.
- [Recipe: Scan Bytes with SIMD](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/simd-scan.md): The five-step pattern that changes a loop of one byte at a time into a scan as wide as a register.
- [Recipe: Vector Algebra](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/vector-algebra.md): Dot, length, normalize and cross on @Vector, written as math and not as loops.
- [Recipe: Keep the Last N Items](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/ring-buffer.md): A generic ring buffer with a fixed capacity, built with a type function.
- [Recipe: Set Operations on the Cheap](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/bitsets.md): A static bit set does membership, intersection and union with one instruction each.
- [Recipe: Reproducible Randomness](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/seeded-random.md): Seeded generators make random worlds, tests and replays repeatable.
- [Recipe: Split Work Across Threads](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/parallel-sum.md): Divide a slice among threads with no locks and one join.
- [Recipe: An Atomic Work Index](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/work-index.md): Dynamic load balancing with fetchAdd, without locks or chunks.
- [Recipe: A Producer/Consumer Queue](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/worker-queue.md): std.Io.Queue as a bounded channel, with close() as the shutdown protocol.
- [Recipe: Struct Memory Layout](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/memory-layout.md): Read the size, alignment and field offsets that a struct really gets, and control them.

**Databases**

- [Recipe: SQLite From Zig](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/databases/sqlite-basic.md): Open a database, create a table, insert with a prepared statement, and query, through the C API.
- [Recipe: A Redis RESP Round Trip](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/databases/redis-resp.md): Use the RESP protocol of Redis over a socket, with a small server and client in one process.
- [Recipe: The PostgreSQL Wire Protocol](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/how-to/databases/postgres-wire.md): Use the Postgres protocol directly, and frame a startup handshake and a query by hand.

## From Scratch

Rebuild the tools that you use every day, one program at a time, with only code that you wrote.

### Survive the Terminal

The primitives that a shell needs: string length, comparison, copy and trim written by hand, a command-line tokenizer, and the read-eval-print loop.

- [String Primitives](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/terminal/strings.md): strlen, compare, copy and trim, written out. The off-by-one error occurs in these functions.
- [Tokenize a Command Line](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/terminal/tokenize.md): Change "ls -la /tmp" into the argv that a shell needs, and copy nothing.
- [The Read-Eval-Print Loop](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/terminal/repl.md): Four steps and two ways to stop. Programmers often get the stop wrong.

### Unix Tools

Rebuild the standard Unix tools in Zig: cat, wc, grep, sort, cut, printf and make. Each chapter is one complete program that runs in the page.

- [cat](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/unix-tools/cat.md): A loop around one fixed buffer. For this reason, cat can copy a file that is larger than memory.
- [wc](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/unix-tools/wc.md): To count words, count each time that the input goes into a word.
- [grep](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/unix-tools/grep.md): Search is a loop over start positions, and the exit code is the answer.
- [sort](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/unix-tools/sort.md): To sort lines is easy. To own the lines is the part that has a cost.
- [cut](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/unix-tools/cut.md): How to split a line at a delimiter, and the edge cases that decide if the split is correct.
- [printf](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/unix-tools/printf.md): How to change a number into text, one digit at a time, from the last digit to the first.
- [make](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/unix-tools/make.md): A dependency graph, a topological order, and a comparison of timestamps.

### Tiny Language

Build a small language from zero: a lexer, a recursive descent parser, a tree-walking interpreter, call frames, a bytecode compiler and a VM.

- [A Lexer](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/tiny-lang/lexer.md): The lexer changes characters into tokens. It looks one character ahead and never moves back in the source.
- [A Parser](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/tiny-lang/parser.md): One function for each precedence level. Each function calls the function for the next tighter level.
- [A Tree-Walking Interpreter](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/tiny-lang/interpreter.md): To evaluate a node, evaluate its children and then combine the results.
- [Functions and Frames](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/tiny-lang/functions.md): A call needs a place for its own variables, and a way to return to the caller.
- [A Bytecode Compiler](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/tiny-lang/compiler.md): The compiler walks the same tree one time at compile time, not one time for each run.
- [A Virtual Machine](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/tiny-lang/vm.md): Fetch, decode, execute. A loop over an array, with no tree.
- [A Calling Convention](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/tiny-lang/calls.md): Where the arguments go, which side removes them, and how the machine returns to the caller.

### Web Server

Parse an HTTP request by hand, format a response, and send it over a real socket. HTTP is text, a blank line ends the headers, and you need no framework.

- [Parse an HTTP Request](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/web-server/request.md): A request line, some headers, a blank line. The blank line is the difficult part.
- [An HTTP Server](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/web-server/server.md): The parser from the last chapter, with a socket in front of the parser.
- [Serve Files Safely](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/web-server/static.md): Decode first, then check. The opposite order is the bug.
- [Routes and Query Strings](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/web-server/routes.md): All text after the question mark, and the dispatch table that ignores that text.
- [Form Bodies](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/web-server/forms.md): The same encoding as a query string, but in the body, where it can be much larger.
- [Cookies and Sessions](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/web-server/sessions.md): A cookie is a string that the client stores and sends back. All the rest is policy.
- [A Template Engine](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/web-server/templates.md): Substitution is the easy half. Escaping by default is the more difficult half.
- [File Uploads](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/web-server/multipart.md): A format where the client selects the delimiter, and a filename that you cannot trust until you check it.

### Data and Storage

How storage engines work: an append-only log, the lost update from two writers, indexes that change a scan to a lookup, and a crash-safe write-ahead log.

- [An Append-Only Record Store](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/storage/flatdb.md): Never modify written data. A delete is a record that you add.
- [Two Writers, One File](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/storage/filelock.md): What a lost update looks like, and the lock that prevents it.
- [An Index Over the Log](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/storage/indexes.md): A second structure, made from the first, that you must now keep in agreement with the first.
- [A Write-Ahead Log](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/storage/kvstore.md): Write down what you will do, then do it. Recovery is a replay of the note.
- [A Query Engine](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/storage/minidb.md): The parser asks what. The planner asks how, and the planner does the real work of a database.

### The Browser

The pipeline behind each web page: an HTML parser that cannot fail, CSS matching, a layout engine that makes boxes, and a renderer that makes pixels.

- [An HTML Parser](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/browser/html.md): A format with no parse errors, because the first browsers made that decision.
- [A Stylesheet and the Cascade](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/browser/css.md): To match a rule is easy. The cascade is the decision about which match wins.
- [Layout](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/browser/layout.md): The parent gives each child its width. The children add up to the height of the parent.
- [Paint](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/browser/render.md): A rectangle of memory, filled from back to front. The last write wins.
- [A Scripting Engine](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/browser/script.md): The language knows nothing about documents. The host makes the connection between them.
- [The Whole Pipeline](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/browser/browser.md): Bytes, tree, styles, boxes, pixels. Five stages, in one direction.

## Projects

One library at a time, designed in public, with one decision in each chapter.

### An Ecto-Style ORM

An Ecto-style ORM in Zig: schemas as types, a typed query builder, migrations as data, errdefer transactions, and an adapter seam for SQLite and Postgres.

- [What Is an Ecto-Style ORM?](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/orm/what-is-ecto.md): The Elixir design that these chapters copy, explained for readers who never wrote Elixir.
- [A Type Function as the Front Door](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/orm/schema-to-sql.md): The central pattern of a Zig library: take the type of the caller, and return a richer type.
- [A Typed Query Builder](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/orm/query-builder.md): Compile-time field checks and output that stops injection, with no allocator.
- [Validation from Declarations](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/orm/validation-rules.md): Optional capabilities found with @hasDecl, the convention-over-configuration of Zig.
- [Write Rows](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/orm/insert-update.md): INSERT and UPDATE statements derived from the schema, with the values in a typed array.
- [The Adapter Seam](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/orm/adapters.md): One query renderer, several SQL dialects, resolved at compile time.
- [Migrations as Data](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/orm/migrations.md): The schema history as an append-only list, and a pure plan that applies it.
- [The Repo](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/orm/repo.md): The composition root, and the fake driver that lets you test the full ORM.
- [Transactions and errdefer](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/orm/transactions.md): COMMIT on success, ROLLBACK on each error path, enforced by four lines.

### A URL Shortener

A CRUD web service in Zig with no framework and no database driver: the PostgreSQL wire protocol, base62 slugs, and HTTP handlers on plain bytes.

- [What You Will Build](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/url-shortener/what-we-are-building.md): A URL shortener with real storage, and the two decisions that control all the chapters after this one.
- [A Postgres Client](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/url-shortener/pg-client.md): Startup, password auth, a row iterator and error recovery, with tests against scripted bytes.
- [Slugs Are Arithmetic](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/url-shortener/slugs.md): Base62 over the row id, and the validation that a redirect service needs.
- [Routes Over a Seam](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/url-shortener/routes.md): All five CRUD routes as one pure function, with tests against an in-memory store.
- [The Server](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/url-shortener/the-server.md): The client, the slugs and the routes put together into one file, and run against a real Postgres.

### Lane Dodger

A hyper casual game in Zig and raylib that you play in the page: vendored C, a fixed timestep, handles, a derived difficulty curve and synthesised sound.

- [A Game You Can Test](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/lane-dodger/what-we-are-building.md): A three lane endless runner that you can play here, and the one rule that lets you test the rest.
- [Vendor raylib](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/lane-dodger/the-build.md): How to add raylib to a Zig project, why this project uses the C source, and how the game gets to a browser canvas.
- [The World](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/lane-dodger/the-world.md): A field with its own units, a player that slides between lanes, and the order of the work in a tick.
- [The Loop Takes No dt](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/lane-dodger/the-loop.md): A fixed timestep, an accumulator, interpolation for the leftover time, and the split that the browser build needs.
- [Handles, Not Pointers](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/lane-dodger/entities.md): A pool with a fixed capacity and generational handles, and the event stream that the particles and the sound use.
- [Draw It](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/lane-dodger/drawing.md): Field units mapped onto a window, the road, the entities, and a particle system that contains no raylib types.
- [Input](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/lane-dodger/input.md): The game latches presses one time in each frame and gives each press to exactly one tick. A held key must not cross the board.
- [Difficulty You Can Prove](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/lane-dodger/fair-by-design.md): Row spacing from what is physically possible, a bot that proves that the course is solvable, and a reaction time model for playability.
- [Sound Without Sound Files](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/lane-dodger/sound.md): Five effects that the game synthesises at startup from oscillators and envelopes, and waveform tests that run without an audio device.
- [Build It From Scratch](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/lane-dodger/build-it.md): The order in which to write the files, the two points where you can stop and check, and what to do when the build fails.

### A Paint Program

A paint program in Zig that runs in the page, with no graphics library: brushes, a 16-bit stroke buffer, layers, undo, flood fill and PNG export.

- [A Paint Program You Can Test](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/paint/a-paint-program.md): A paint program that you can use on this page, and the one rule that lets tests check each brush.
- [Strokes](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/paint/strokes.md): Pointer samples come at irregular distances. Move along the path, put a dab at a fixed distance, and keep the distance that remains for the next segment.
- [Smoothing, Pressure and Scatter](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/paint/smoothing-pressure-scatter.md): Make a shaky hand steady with a moving average. Get the size of each dab from pen pressure. Scatter dabs with a random generator that repeats.
- [The Tip](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/paint/the-tip.md): A dab is a disc with a soft edge. Make it an ellipse, turn it, and the same twenty lines draw a soft brush, a calligraphy nib and a ribbon.
- [Bristles and Paper](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/paint/bristles-and-paper.md): A row of thin hairs across the stroke gives separate tracks. A fixed grid of paper heights decides where a dry brush touches.
- [Oil: Pickup and Paint Load](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/paint/oil.md): An oil brush carries paint. It collects some of the colour below it, and it becomes dry as it moves.
- [Flow and Opacity](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/paint/flow-and-opacity.md): Dabs overlap. Put the coverage of a stroke in its own buffer and apply its opacity at the end. Then a stroke at 50% stays at 50% where it crosses itself.
- [Layers and the Eraser](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/paint/layers-and-the-eraser.md): Layers are transparent pixel arrays on white paper. Store them premultiplied, and the eraser becomes one multiplication.
- [Undo](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/paint/undo.md): Keep only the changed rectangle. Undo and redo are one swap, two stacks are an array and an index, and a memory failure costs an undo step, not the stroke.
- [Fill](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/paint/fill.md): A flood fill finds its area a small number of pixels at a time. A queue and a visited map do this in fixed memory. Recursion uses all of the stack.
- [Save a PNG](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/paint/saving.md): The program flattens the picture onto white paper and writes it as a PNG. Each row gets the filter, of five, that makes its bytes smallest.
- [Projects and Presets](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/paint/projects-and-presets.md): A project file keeps the layers that a PNG merges. A preset keeps a brush. Other people can write both, thus the program examines both first.
- [Watercolour](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/paint/watercolour.md): Water and pigment on a grid of paper. They spread, the paper dries, and pigment settles into it. Fixed steps make each run the same on all computers.
- [A Native Window](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/paint/a-native-window.md): The same engine in a desktop window with raylib. Linux builds for Windows with one flag. A licence, not the compiler, stops a build for macOS.

### A Chat Server

A WebSocket chat server in Zig with only the standard library: a text protocol, a hub with one outbox for each member, slow clients, and frames.

- [What You Will Build](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/chat-server/what-we-are-building.md): A chat room over WebSocket with only the standard library, and the four decisions that the next chapters make.
- [The Protocol](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/chat-server/protocol.md): Commands in, events out. A text protocol inside WebSocket messages, a tagged union for each direction, and a line size that the compiler checks.
- [The Hub](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/chat-server/hub.md): One writer for each socket. The hub keeps the members, copies each line into a bounded outbox, and never touches a socket.
- [Slow Clients](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/chat-server/slow-clients.md): A member that does not read fills its outbox. The hub puts with a minimum of 0, drops the member when nothing fits, and the room does not wait.
- [Read the Frames Yourself](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/chat-server/frames.md): A frame reader for the server. It joins fragments, returns the close code, checks UTF-8 and the size, and maps each failure to a close code.
- [The Server](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/chat-server/the-server.md): The protocol, the hub and the frame reader on real sockets. A reader task and a writer task for each connection, and three clients that chat.

## Practice

The algorithms that a contest problem expects you to know. Each program prints the steps that it took.

### Competitive Programming

Contest algorithms in Zig, one complete program per chapter. Each program prints its steps, from binary search and two pointers to knapsack.

- [Binary Search](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/competitive-programming/binary-search.md): The half-open window, the invariant that keeps the window correct, and the two bounds that std already has.
- [Two Pointers](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/competitive-programming/two-pointers.md): Two indices that start at opposite ends, and the argument that tells which index must move.
- [Sliding Window](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/competitive-programming/sliding-window.md): One addition and one subtraction instead of a new sum, the window that grows and shrinks, and the count that shows the total stays linear.
- [Prefix Sums and Difference Arrays](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/competitive-programming/prefix-sums.md): One subtraction instead of a loop, an extra cell for index 0, and the same method in reverse for range updates.
- [The Monotonic Stack](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/competitive-programming/monotonic-stack.md): A stack of the indices that still wait for an answer, and the two counters that show the inner loop keeps the total linear.
- [Binary Search on the Answer](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/competitive-programming/binary-search-answer.md): Search a range of possible answers instead of an array, with a greedy pack as the predicate and a full scan to check the boundary.
- [Breadth-First Search on a Grid](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/competitive-programming/grid-bfs.md): The distance field as the frontier grows, and the one line with a position that decides if a cell can enter the queue two times.
- [Merge Intervals](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/competitive-programming/merge-intervals.md): A sort by start for one pass, the nested interval that shortens a run without @max, and a sweep that counts open intervals.
- [The Monotonic Deque](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/competitive-programming/monotonic-deque.md): The largest value in each window, from a deque with two ends that remove indices for two different reasons.
- [Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union)](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/competitive-programming/union-find.md): Groups that merge when edges arrive. A merge moves one root in a parent array, and a find follows links to the root.
- [Take or Skip: The 0/1 Knapsack](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/competitive-programming/knapsack.md): All subsets, the take-or-skip recursion, the table that stops repeats, the walk back to the items, and the one-row version with its loop direction.
- [A Contest Template](https://www.ziglang.in/learn/competitive-programming/contest-template.md): The one program in the section that reads real stdin, and three problems that a judge finds and a browser never shows.
